prompt.context: Your client is an office supplies retailer in the Boston area. The client currently serves mainly large businesses. The business has been pretty flat lately, with little to no growth.
prompt.question: Your client wants to find ways to increase growth. How would you approach this?

clarifying_info.q: What geography does the client serve, and are they open to expanding?
clarifying_info.a: The client currently operates in the Boston area and wants to stay in the Boston area.
The business currently serves large clients in the Boston area.

clarifying_info.q: Does the client have its own distribution capabilities?
clarifying_info.a: The client owns its own truck fleet for distribution.

clarifying_info.q: Does the client have a sales force?
clarifying_info.a: Yes, the client has its own sales force.

exhibits.title: Sales and Cost Comparison: Large vs. SMB Clients
exhibits.shows: A table comparing Large clients vs. SMB clients across three metrics: Average Sales, Time needed to close sale, and Cost of salesperson per day.

framework: Assess organic growth options with current customers and current products (e.g., volume discounts, loyalty programs, lower prices)
Assess new product options for current customers (e.g., new product lines such as home/garden or electronics)
Assess new customer segments with current products (e.g., expand to Small/Medium Businesses, attract additional large businesses, expand online presence)
Assess new customer + new product combinations (e.g., online expansion, advertising, partnerships)
Evaluate each option by profitability potential, investment required, risk level, and fit with existing capabilities (truck fleet, sales force)
Recommend best option(s) with supporting rationale; interviewer should steer toward SMB expansion as lowest-risk given existing distribution and sales infrastructure

questions.prompt: What could be some problems with pursuing Small/Medium Businesses?
questions.guidance: Candidate should brainstorm in a structured way using two main buckets — Profitability Considerations and Operational Considerations. Profitability: more and smaller deliveries result in higher delivery cost structure; competition with established players already serving SMBs. Operational: fewer products per shipment for SMBs; fewer existing connections/leads with SMBs; changes needed in the salesforce to reach SMBs. After discussion, share that preliminary assessments show there is an SMB market large enough for the client to enter in Boston.

questions.prompt: Using Exhibit 1, calculate the financial viability of pursuing Small/Medium Businesses versus staying focused on Large clients.
questions.guidance: Candidate should compare revenue generated per salesperson relative to the cost of that salesperson. The key insight is that large clients are more profitable per salesperson-day, but SMBs are not dramatically worse and the client faces flat growth in the large segment. A strong candidate will note that flat sales in the large segment suggests the client may have captured most available market share there, making SMB expansion still worthwhile despite slightly lower profitability.

math.setup: Compare sales per salesperson over a common time period. Use 4-day period as the common denominator (time to close a Large deal). Salesperson cost is $50/day.
steps: Large: $10K sales per salesperson over 4 days; salesperson cost = 4 days x $50 = $200. Net = $10,000 - $200 = $9,800
SMB: $2K sales per salesperson per day; over 4 days = 4 deals x $2K = $8K sales; salesperson cost = 4 days x $50 = $200. Net = $8,000 - $200 = $7,800
Alternatively per day: Large = $2,500 sales/day vs $50 cost; SMB = $2,000 sales/day vs $50 cost
Large clients yield more revenue per salesperson ($10K vs $8K over 4-day period) at the same cost ($200)
math.answer: Large clients are more profitable per salesperson ($9,800 net vs $7,800 net over 4 days). However, since the large-client market is saturated (flat growth), SMB expansion is still justified — the cost of sales is the same and SMBs provide access to an untapped addressable market.

brainstorming.prompt: What are potential growth options available to the client?

categories.name: Current Customers / Current Products
ideas: Offer volume discounts to incentivize larger orders
Institute loyalty programs to increase retention and repeat purchases
Lower prices or offer promotional discounts to increase wallet share

categories.name: Current Customers / New Products
ideas: R&D investment to develop new product lines
Offer new lines such as home/garden or electronics to existing large-business accounts

categories.name: New Customers / Current Products
ideas: Expand to Small and Medium Businesses (lowest risk given existing truck fleet and sales force)
Attract additional large businesses through targeted outreach
Expand online presence to reach customers outside current sales channels
Increase advertising to build brand awareness

recommendation: Expand to serve Small and Medium Businesses in the Boston area — this is the easiest and lowest-risk growth path given existing distribution infrastructure (truck fleet) and sales force
Continue to maintain and grow the large-client business, as large clients are more profitable per salesperson; do not neglect this segment
risks: New and existing competitors already established in the SMB market
Difficulty reaching SMB clients with whom the client has no prior relationship
Potential need to adjust the logistics network to accommodate more frequent, smaller-volume deliveries, which could be costly or operationally disruptive
next_steps: Conduct further market research to size the SMB market in the Boston area and identify key segments
Focus salesforce on generating leads and building pipelines in the SMB market
Evaluate whether logistics network adjustments are needed for smaller-order fulfillment
